title: Two bird drought rank tests had only four shared species in six abundance samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested support for species response rankings across bird drought studies. Six abundance samples in a 2024 public release contain 179 records and 143 species names. Only eight species occur in two studies. Thirteen of 15 study pairs have no common species. Two Australian pairs each share four species and have rank correlations of -0.8 and +1.0. Exact two-sided permutation probabilities are 0.3333 and 0.0833. Even perfect agreement among four untied ranks cannot pass a 0.05 threshold with this test. A broader abundance selection leaves the overlap limit unchanged. The result is a limit of the evidence and specified test, not evidence that sensitivity fails to transfer. Species-label exchangeability, exact name matching and correct source extraction are necessary assumptions. Detection bias, different metrics, shared events and incomplete dates limit inference. No balanced independent-period validation or air pollution test is supported. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Shared species counts and the smallest attainable two-sided rank permutation probability. Only two pairs share species, with four species each. The curves are exact test limits for untied ranks, not confidence intervals or power estimates.
